senses.definition: A long island near a coast that can shelter the water and land behind it from some ocean waves.
senses.example: A sandy barrier island lay between the open ocean and the quiet sound.

senses.definition: A broad area of low, often fairly flat land beside an ocean or another large body of water.
senses.example: The river flowed slowly across the coastal plain before reaching the sea.

senses.definition: A line of higher ground that separates river systems draining to different oceans or major basins.
senses.example: Rain falling on different sides of a continental divide can end up far apart.

senses.definition: All the land where water runs toward the same river, lake or other low place.
senses.example: The streams in the same drainage basin eventually reached one river.

senses.definition: An area set apart from the surrounding states for the government of a whole country.
senses.example: Washington, D.C., is the federal district at the seat of the U.S. government.

senses.definition: Loose rock and soil that a glacier or its meltwater leaves behind.
senses.example: Glacial drift covered some of the rock that the ice once crossed.

senses.definition: The place where a river flows into a lake, sea or another body of water.
senses.example: The wide bay began near the river mouth.

senses.definition: Low land shaped in part by a river, often between hills or higher land.
senses.example: Hills rose on both sides of the wide river valley.

senses.definition: A hill or ridge of loose sand built up by wind.
senses.example: Grass grew along the side of the sand dune above the beach.

senses.definition: A place deep below Earth’s surface that can supply molten rock to build volcanoes.
senses.example: As a plate moved across a volcanic hot spot, a line of volcanoes formed.
